2. In the Graphic sub-tab, set the values the properties should end at.

While an action is selected, the Properties rows edit the action's end.
Numbers and colours ramp across the action, colours blending through OKLab.
Text, checkboxes, menus and pictures switch at the action's end, and their
rows say "at end". A value written to an action's end is stored as given,
even when it equals the module's default. A property the module marks as not
animatable still edits the clip itself. Size and Timeline always edit the
clip.

The Graphic sub-tab's badge counts how many properties the selected action
animates. A property the action names that the module no longer declares, or
no longer lets be animated, shows dimmed with **⌫** to take it out of the
action.

An animated number arrives in the module with decimals (64 to 129 is 96.5
halfway). A module that needs whole numbers must round them. See
[the API reference](../graphics-api.md#animating-a-prop-from-the-timeline).

*Agents:* `add_action`, then `set_action_end` with
`{graphic: {props: {…}}}` in its patch.

## Copying properties between graphic clips

**Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties** (no shortcut) pastes a copied graphic
clip's properties, text and colours included, onto every selected clip drawn
by the same module. Each target keeps its own size, In and Length. Selected
clips drawn by another module, or that aren't graphics, are skipped. If none
can take the paste, it beeps.

**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (⌥⌘V) does not carry graphic properties.

Copying and pasting a graphic clip (⌘C, ⌘V) pastes a clip that names its
module; the module's `.js` file, fonts and pictures are not copied. In a
project without that module, the pasted clip draws the red error card until
you add the module under the same name, for example with **Insert ▸ Graphic…**'s
**From File…** on a file of that name.

*Agents:* `paste_attributes` with `groups: ["graphic"]`.

## Fonts and pictures

**File ▸ Add Font to Graphics…** copies a `.ttf` or `.otf` file into the
project's `graphics/fonts/`. Every graphic in the project can then use it. A
file that loads no face is refused, and a file with the same name replaces
the old one. Nothing is shown when it works.

The family name a module must use is the one the graphics engine reads from
the file, which can differ from the name Font Book or other apps show. If a
font doesn't draw, the Source section reports the missing font; an agent's
`get_graphic {}` or `import_graphic_font` answer lists the exact family
names.

Graphics also have these bundled families: Anton, Bebas Neue, Darker
Grotesque, IBM Plex Mono, Montserrat, Source Sans 3 and Source Serif 4. The
generic `serif`, `sans-serif` and `monospace` draw in Source Serif 4, Source
Sans 3 and IBM Plex Mono.

**File ▸ Add Image to Graphics…** copies a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG or SVGZ
picture into `graphics/assets/`, where a module can draw it and an asset
property's pop-up lists it. Any other kind of file, and an empty file, is
refused. A file with the same name replaces the old one. A file name a module
can't refer to (one starting with `.` or `#`, or holding `/ : " ' < > &` or a
control character, or longer than 247 bytes) is added under a legal name, and
a notice says which; a renamed copy never replaces an existing file, but
takes `-2`, `-3` and so on.

Neither import is an undo step.

*Agents:* `import_graphic_font` (answers `families`, the exact names
`font-family` must use, `library_families`, every family now available, and
`replaced`) and `import_graphic_asset` (answers `name`, the name to pass to
`asset()`, `renamed_from` when the name was made legal, `replaced`, and every
asset in the folder).

## Editing a module

A module is an ordinary file in the project package's `graphics/` folder.
You can edit it in any editor (**Open in Editor** in the Source section) or
with your own tools. Frame Job watches the folder: when a module, font or
picture changes, the paused preview redraws and the inspector updates within
a moment, and a playing preview picks the change up on its next frame.

The folder is created the first time something is written to it. Frame Job
also keeps `API.md` and `API.d.ts` there, the reference and its type
definitions, for an editor or an agent working in the folder. **Help ▸
Graphics Reference** opens the same reference in your default Markdown app,
with or without a project open.

In an untitled project, graphics are kept in a temporary folder and move into
the package when you first save it.

### Kept versions

Whenever Frame Job sees a module's code replaced while the project is open
(an agent's write, a save from your editor, a restore), it keeps the code
that was there. The last 10 versions of each module are kept in
`graphics/history/`. Leave that folder to Frame Job.

## Renaming, deleting and restoring graphics

The **File** menu has three items that each open a small sheet with a
**Graphic:** pop-up of the project's modules:

| Item | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Rename Graphic…** | Renames the module. Type a **New name:** (lowercase letters, digits and -). Every clip drawn by it, on the timeline and inside nests, follows the new name. The field starts with the chosen module's name and changes when you pick another; **Rename** stays disabled until the name is not empty and differs from the current one |
| **Delete Graphic…** | Deletes a module that no clip uses. Its code is kept, so it can be restored |
| **Restore Graphic Version…** | Puts back the newest kept version of a module's code, deleted modules included (listed as "name (deleted)"). The sheet says how many versions are kept |

Rename and Restore open on the selected clip's module when one clip is
selected. Delete always opens on the first module in the list.

- **Rename** is one undo step when a clip uses the module, and Undo renames
  the file back too. A module no clip uses is renamed back by renaming it
  again. Rename is refused if the new name isn't a module name, if a module
  of that name already exists, or if clips left behind by a deleted module of
  that name still use it. Rename is greyed while a nest is open.
- **Delete** is refused while any clip is drawn by the module, and the sheet
  names those clips: delete them or switch them to another module first.
  Fonts and pictures are left alone. Deleting is not an undo step.
- **Switching clips to another module**: the inspector can't point clips at
  a different existing module. **Duplicate as New Graphic…** only switches
  them to a new copy. To move clips to a module that already exists, delete
  the clips and insert that module again, or have an agent call
  `set_graphic` with `{clips, patch: {name}}`.
- **Restore** keeps the code it replaces, so restoring again returns to where
  you were. Restoring is not an undo step.

On success the sheet closes without a message. A refusal beeps and appears
in the sheet in Frame Job's own words, and the sheet stays open. Rename and Delete are greyed in a project with no graphics, and Restore
when no version of any graphic is kept.

*Agents:* `rename_graphic` (`name`, `to`), `delete_graphic` (`name`),
`restore_graphic` (`name`, and optionally a `revision` from `kept`, where the
menu always restores the newest).

## Showing video inside a graphic

A graphic can't read a video's pixels, but it can shape one. Put the graphic
on the track directly above the video and set that track to a matte with
**Track ▸ Matte**. The video then shows only where the graphic draws (or,
inverted, where it doesn't). See [Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md)
for the matte modes and the
[API reference](../graphics-api.md#video-inside-a-graphic-the-matte) for an
example module.

## Playback, rendering and memory

- **While playing forward**, Frame Job draws upcoming graphic frames on spare
  processor cores ahead of the playhead, and keeps frames it has drawn in
  memory while the window is open, so a stretch you play again comes from
  memory.
- **Background render**: when you leave Frame Job alone, the window you last
  used draws its graphics ahead of the paused playhead, so the next play is
  smooth from the start. A click, a key, an edit, or play, pause or seek in
  any Frame Job window (an agent's edits and playhead moves included) stops
  it at once, and it starts again after the same wait. Moving the pointer
  alone, or working in another app, doesn't stop it. It never runs while a
  window is playing, and it keeps the processor busy while it runs.

  | Setting (Settings ▸ Playback) | What it does | Default |
  |---|---|---|
  | Background render | Turns background drawing on or off | On |
  | Start after … seconds | How long Frame Job must be left alone first, 1–60 | 5 |

  See [Settings](settings.md).
- **Memory**: the drawn frames held ahead and kept use at most a quarter of
  your Mac's memory, and less when memory is short. They are let go when the
  window closes or newer frames replace them.
- **A graphic that fails** (its module is missing, doesn't compile, throws,
  or runs too long) draws a dark red error card with the error's text in
  place of the graphic, in the preview and in stills.
- **Time budget**: each frame has 250 ms to draw in the preview and 2 s in an
  export.
- **HDR projects**: in an HDR (HLG) project, graphics are drawn at HDR
  reference white (203 cd/m²), like titles and shapes, so a white graphic
  matches SDR white rather than reaching into the highlights. See
  [HDR and colour](hdr-and-color.md).

## Exporting

An export draws each graphic as its module stood when the export was queued.
Editing a module while an export runs doesn't change that file. See
[Export](export.md).

- An export that would draw a graphic whose module is missing or doesn't
  compile is not started. The message names each graphic and its first error.
- A graphic that fails partway through stops the export at that frame, names
  the graphic, and writes no file.
- Warnings a graphic gives while drawing don't stop the export. An agent's
  export result lists them as `graphic_warnings`.

## Working with an agent

An agent connected over MCP (see [MCP](mcp.md)) can do the whole job:

1. `graphic_reference`: read the API once. No project needs to be open.
2. `write_graphic {name, source}`: write `graphics/<name>.js`. The answer is
   the compile of that exact text: `ok`, the module's `meta` and `schema`,
   and `diagnostics` with line and column. A module that doesn't compile is an
   answer with `ok: false`, not an error: fix it and write again. Clips
   already drawn by the module redraw at once.
3. `render_graphic {name, frames}`: look at up to 16 frames on a contact sheet
   (a PNG with each frame's number under it) without placing a clip; `frame`
   draws one frame instead (not with `frames`; with neither, frame 0). A frame
   that fails is drawn as its error card, with a sentence giving the engine's
   location. `format: "svg"` answers one frame's SVG text, its diagnostics and
   the `ctx` it was drawn with. It takes `props`, `width`,
   `height`, `max_width` (default 2048), `background` (`transparent`, the
   default, `checker`, or a hex colour) and `path`. A sheet draws at most
   134,217,728 pixels of frames in all.
4. `import_graphic_font {path}` and `import_graphic_asset {path, name?}`: add
   a font or a picture.
5. `add_graphic_clip`: place it. `set_graphic` changes it, and
   `add_action` with `set_action_end` animates it.
6. `render_frame`: check a frame of the timeline.

`get_graphic {name}` reads one module: its source, revision, compile result,
the clips it draws, and `kept`, its kept revisions, newest first.
`get_graphic {}` reads the folder: its path (and whether it exists yet), every
module with its revision, `ok` and clips, the font families and pictures
available, the scan's `warnings`, and `history`, every name with kept
versions, deleted modules included. An agent may also edit the folder with
its own file tools; the app sees the change within a moment.

File writes (`write_graphic`, `restore_graphic`, `delete_graphic` and the
imports) are not undo steps and don't mark the project edited. Placing and
changing clips, and `rename_graphic`'s change to the clips, are undo steps.

## Limits

- A graphic draws at most 8192 pixels on a side.
- Properties show only when all the selected clips share one module, and
  Timeline only for a single clip.
- A clip stores at most 64 property values.
- Rename Graphic… is unavailable while a nest is open.
- Delete Graphic… is refused while any clip, including one inside a nest,
  uses the module.
- Only the last 10 versions of each module are kept.
- Frame Job watches the first 16 module, font and picture files one by one. In
  a folder with more, a save that rewrites a later file in place may not show
  until something else in the folder changes.
- The memory used for drawn frames is capped at a quarter of the Mac's.

projects projects/new-project-from-range | New Project from Range | Keeping only a range as a new project: clips cut at the edges, the caches, graphics and transcripts it brings along, its naming and undo, and what refuses it.
editing editing/add-clips | Add clips to the timeline | Dragging a media row to a track, the canvas or past the stack; new clips covering the whole file and fitting the canvas; where a drop lands; and drops that spring back. Text, shape and graphic clips have their own pages.
editing editing/trimming | Trim clips | Dragging an edge, W and E to trim to the playhead, the Trim buttons, footage bounds, text and graphics trimming to any length, and how a trim treats actions. Rate stretch is on speed/rate-stretch.
editing editing/splitting | Split clips | Split at the playhead from the key or the button, footage staying continuous, and what happens to actions, word timings and graphics.
editing editing/copy-and-paste | Copy, cut and paste | Copy, Cut and Paste of clips: the copied arrangement, where it lands, pasting between projects, a detached sound coming along, paste never refused for room, and copied clips as text.
editing editing/paste-attributes | Paste Attributes | Copying a clip's settings to others in groups (Video, Audio, Text, Shape), what it carries (grade, LUT, cursor) and what it leaves alone (actions, speed, graphic properties), skipped clips and refusals.
canvas canvas/select-on-canvas | Select on the canvas | Clicking layers in the preview, ⇧-click, clicking the void to deselect, the selection frame and handles, and matte clips.
canvas canvas/matte-tracks | Matte tracks | Making a track cut the one behind it: Alpha, Inverted Alpha, Luma and Inverted Luma, the Matte submenu, matte track chrome and notes, gaps, matte properties, sound, an adjustment clip on a matte, and turning a matte off.
canvas canvas/mattes-in-nests | Mattes inside nests | What happens to a matte when you nest, un-nest or transition across matted tracks. Video inside a graphic is on graphics/video-inside-a-graphic.
text-and-shapes text-and-shapes/text-style | Font and text style | The Text tab's Font and Style sections: Family, Style, Size, Color, Align, Vertical, UPPERCASE, Line spacing and Tracking.
text-and-shapes text-and-shapes/fonts | Fonts | Which fonts text clips can use: installed fonts and the faces the app ships with. Fonts inside graphics are on graphics/fonts-and-pictures.
effects effects/text-behind-subject | Text Behind Subject | Putting a title behind the person in a clip: the Behind Subject section, what it needs from the cut-out, and clip order.
motion motion/what-can-animate | What an action can animate | Which properties ramp, which switch at the end, and which can't animate at all, across Picture, Text, Sound, Color, Graphic and Speed, and colours blending in OKLab.
audio audio/voice-isolation | Voice Isolation | Isolating speech on this Mac, with de-reverb: Amount, Status, the background render, speed limits, and a failed render.
audio audio/voice-effects | Voice effects | The sixteen effects in the Voice Effect popup (Voice, Tone, Space and Character groups), Amount, Pitch, Status and the background render.
color color/adjustment-clips | Adjustment clips | Insert Adjustment Clip: a clip that grades everything behind it, Strength, its span and track, the limits (no nests, transitions, Picture tab), and confining it with a matte.
color color/copy-a-grade | Copy a grade | Paste Attributes for a grade: what it carries, LUTs travelling with it, a qualifier between adjustment clips, and pastes refused. The command itself is on editing/paste-attributes.
framing framing/vertical-what-changes | What Make Vertical changes | Clip by clip: full-frame movies follow their subject, screen recordings follow the pointer, camera layouts are re-laid, word captions re-paged, graphics re-sized, stills and nests centred, and everything else kept as placed.
recording recording/cursor-settings | Style the recorded cursor | The Picture tab's Cursor section: Show cursor, Size, Style, Smoothing, Hide when idle, Clicks and Ripple, Polish, Reset, actions, Paste Attributes and motion blur.
recording recording/shortcut-overlays | Shortcut overlays | Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays: the Shortcuts track, Keyboard keys clips, overlay duration, repeats counted, overlays close together, and notices.
export export/what-an-export-includes | What an export includes | The rules every export shares: the same picture and sound as the preview with view-only settings left out, waiting for ramps, masks and analysis, missing media still exporting, graphics as asked, burned-in captions, and colour lab

audio audio/voice-effects | Voice effects | The sixteen effects in the Voice Effect popup (Voice, Tone, Space and Character groups), Amount, Pitch, Status and the background render.

content.content:
# Frame Job graphics — the API

A **graphic** is a motion graphic drawn by code: one JavaScript ES module
whose `render` returns an SVG string for each frame. Frame Job runs it in a
sandboxed QuickJS engine and rasterizes the SVG with resvg. The same frame
with the same props always draws the same pixels. A gradient is dithered
where it is rounded to 8 bits, by a fixed pattern of pixel position under
half a level, so dark gradients do not band; flat colours, images, text and
alpha are not. This page is the whole API. Every `js` block on it is run
by a test, so the examples work as written.

## The module

```js
export const meta = {
  name: "Lower third",        // shown in the inspector
  durationInFrames: 150,      // optional: the default length of a new clip
};

export const schema = {
  title:    { type: "string",  default: "Jane Doe", label: "Title" },
  subtitle: { type: "string",  default: "Director of Photography" },
  accent:   { type: "color",   default: "#ff5a36" },
  size:     { type: "number",  default: 64, min: 12, max: 200, step: 1 },
  boxed:    { type: "boolean", default: true },
  align:    { type: "enum",    default: "left", options: ["left", "center", "right"] },
};

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [-600, 96], { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true });
  const fade = interpolate(frame, [ctx.durationInFrames - 15, ctx.durationInFrames - 1], [1, 0],
    { clamp: true });
  const y = ctx.height - 200;
  return svg(ctx, `
    <g opacity="${fade}">
      ${props.boxed ? `<rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="700" height="150" fill="#101014"/>` : ""}
      <rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="12" height="150" fill="${props.accent}"/>
      <text x="${x + 40}" y="${y}" font-family="Montserrat" font-weight="800"
            font-size="${props.size}" fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(props.title)}</text>
    </g>`);
}
```

- `render(frame, props, ctx)` is required. It must return a string that
  starts with `<svg`; use `svg(ctx, body)` to write the root element.
- `meta` is optional (`{}` when absent). `name` and `durationInFrames` are
  read from it, and two keys only the Insert ▸ Graphic… dialog reads:
  `category`, the list the graphic is filed under (a string; "Other" when
  absent or blank), and `description`, one line shown under the dialog's
  preview. A module in the project's `graphics/` is listed under This
  Project whatever its `category`.
- `schema` is optional (`{}` when absent). It declares the props (below).
- The module is the only source of code: no `import`, no `eval`, no
  `Function`. The standard library below is already global.
- `frame` is an integer counted from the clip's first frame.

## `ctx`

| key | what |
|---|---|
| `fps` | the project's frame rate, e.g. `30` or `29.97002997` |
| `time` | `frame / fps`, in seconds |
| `durationInFrames` | the clip's length in frames |
| `progress` | `frame / max(1, durationInFrames - 1)`, clamped to 0–1 |
| `width`, `height` | the graphic's size in pixels |
| `canvas` | `{width, height}`, the project's canvas |

Write every coordinate in terms of `ctx.width` and `ctx.height` (or a unit
such as `const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080`) so the graphic
draws at any size. That unit is the same as `ctx.height / 1080` on a
landscape canvas, and it keeps a portrait one from drawing 1.78 times too big.

## The schema

At most 64 keys. A key is letters, digits and `_`, starts with a letter or
`_`, and is at most 32 characters. Every entry needs a `type` and a
`default` of that type; `label` (else the key) and `help` (a tooltip) are
optional. Any entry may say `animate: false` (a boolean; absent is `true`):
an action never animates that prop, and the inspector writes it to the clip
even while an action is selected — for a count, a layout mode or a data
series a ramp would break.

| `type` | value | options |
|---|---|---|
| `string` | text, at most 4096 characters | `multiline: true` for a text area |
| `number` | a finite number | `min`, `max`, `step` |
| `boolean` | `true` / `false` | |
| `color` | a CSS colour string: `"#ff5a36"`, `"rgb(255, 90, 54)"`, `"hsl(11, 100%, 61%)"`, `"tomato"` | |
| `enum` | one of `options` | `options`: 1–32 strings |
| `asset` | a file name in `graphics/assets/`, `null` or `""` (no image); `render` gets `null` for either of the last two | `kind: "image"` |

A schema that breaks a rule does not compile, and the error says which rule.
A `color` entry's `default` must be a colour in the grammar
`interpolateColors` lists below, or the module does not compile:
`schema.accent.default "bluish" is not a color`. `props` receives the
default as written, not normalised.
`props` always has every schema key: a stored value replaces the default
only when it fits the type. A value that does not fit is a WARNING, the
default is drawn, and the frame still draws, e.g.
`props.size is a string but the schema says number; the default 64 is used`.

## Fonts

A graphic draws with the fonts bundled with Frame Job, plus any `.ttf` /
`.otf` in the project's `graphics/fonts/`. Never the system's.

| family | weights |
|---|---|
| Anton | 400 |
| Bebas Neue | 400 |
| Darker Grotesque | variable, 300–900 |
| IBM Plex Mono | 400, 500 |
| Montserrat | 800, 900 |
| Source Sans 3 | variable, 200–900 |
| Source Serif 4 | variable, 200–900 |

The CSS generic families draw in bundled faces: `serif` is Source Serif 4,
`sans-serif` is Source Sans 3 and `monospace` is IBM Plex Mono. Write a
generic unquoted (`font-family="sans-serif"`); quoted, it names a family
called "sans-serif", which is not installed. `cursive` and `fantasy` are not
installed.

**Quote a family** in `font-family` or the `font` shorthand when any word
of it starts with a digit: `font-family="'Source Sans 3'"`,
`font: 48px 'Source Sans 3'`. Unquoted, `Source Sans 3` is not a
valid family list: it draws nothing, with a warning. `textLines` quotes
for you. A family the set lacks draws nothing, with a warning naming the
families that are installed; in a list (`"Nope, Montserrat"`) the first
installed family draws.

## The sandbox

A graphic is a pure function of `frame`, `props`, `ctx` and its fonts and
assets. These refuse, with these sentences:

```text
Math.random()        → Math.random is not available; use random(seed)
import x from "x"    → imports are not available in a graphic; the standard library is global
new Function("…")    → Function is not available in a graphic; the module is the one source of code
eval("…")            → ReferenceError: eval is not defined
```

`Date` is frozen: `Date.now()` is `946684800000` and `new Date()` is
2000-01-01T00:00:00Z. There is no `fetch`, file, clock, `performance`,
`WebAssembly` or `Intl`. Modern syntax works: template literals, `??`, `?.`,
`**`, destructuring, `Array.prototype.at`, `replaceAll`, `findLast`.

## Limits

- **Time**: each call has a budget — 250 ms per frame in preview, 2 s in an
  export. The module's top level has one too. Over it, the answer is an
  error such as `over the 250 ms budget at frame 12 (InternalError:
  interrupted)`.
- **Memory**: 64 MB of heap and 1 MB of stack per engine. Past either is an
  error with a line and column.
- **Size**: a graphic draws at most 8192 pixels on a side.
- **The answer**: `render` must return an SVG string. `undefined` is
  ``render returned undefined at frame 12 — did you forget `return`?``.
  The string may be at most 8 MiB (8388608 bytes); a longer one is
  `render returned 9000000 bytes at frame 12; the SVG may be at most
  8388608 bytes`.

## Diagnostics

Every problem comes back as `{level, message, line, column, frame}`.
`level` is `"error"` (nothing drew) or `"warning"` (it drew anyway).
`line` and `column` are the module's own, when known; for a timeout they
are where the function begins, not the statement that ran long. `frame` is
set for a problem found while drawing. A warning from the module's top level
(such as `asset("x")` outside `render`) has no frame, and comes back with the
module's compile: `ok` is still `true`.

## Working over MCP

Read `graphic_reference` once. `write_graphic {name, source}` answers `ok` and
`diagnostics`: write again until `ok` is true. `render_graphic {name, frames}`
draws up to 16 frames on a contact sheet with no clip, at most 134217728
pixels of frames in all (two at 8192×8192, or sixteen at 3840×2160);
`add_graphic_clip {name}` places it, `render_frame` shows a frame,
`set_graphic {patch: {props}}` changes it.
`paste_attributes {clips, payload, groups: ["graphic"]}` copies one clip's props onto other clips
drawn by the same module. `import_graphic_font {path}` answers `families`, the exact names
`font-family` must say; `import_graphic_asset {path}` adds a picture for
`asset(name)`; its `name` is the one to use, and `renamed_from` says it was
renamed. `get_graphic` reads a module or names the folder, which your file
tools may edit too; its `API.md` is this page, `API.d.ts` its types.
`get_graphic {}`'s `warnings` says what the folder's scan skipped or could
not watch, such as a file whose name is not a module name. The app keeps the
last 10 texts of each module whenever it sees one replaced: `kept`, in
`write_graphic`'s and `get_graphic {name}`'s answers, lists their revisions,
newest first, and `get_graphic {}`'s `history` lists every name with a kept
text, deleted modules included. `restore_graphic {name, revision?}` writes a
kept text back (the newest by default) and keeps the one it replaced.
`delete_graphic {name}` removes a module no clip draws and keeps its text, so
`restore_graphic` brings it back. `rename_graphic {name, to}` renames a
module and repoints every clip that draws it as one undo step; undo renames
the file back. The folder's `history/` is the app's: leave it to those three
tools. A successful
`export` answers `graphic_warnings`, each distinct warning a graphic gave
while the file was drawn, with its name and frame.

## Animating a prop from the timeline

A graphic clip's props can be the target of an action, as a clip's position or opacity can:
`add_action {clip, at, duration}` makes the span, and `set_action_end {clip, action, patch:
{graphic: {props: {…}}}}` names the values the props end at. Each value is checked against your
schema as `set_graphic` checks it, `min` and `max` included, using the module as it is now. Across
the action a `number` and a `color` ramp along its curve, a `color` in OKLab, giving the same middle
`interpolateColors` gives; a `string`, `boolean` and `enum` change to the end's value when the
action ends, and an `asset` changes to the end's image when the action ends, `""` naming no image
there (a `null` stops animating the prop); a prop whose entry says `animate: false` cannot be
animated (`set_action_end` refuses a value for it). A prop the clip holds no value
for starts from the schema's `default` as it is when an action first names it, and that value is
written into the clip, so a later change to the default does not move the animation; an asset
whose default is `null` starts from `""`. `render` gets
that frame's values every frame, and your own animation from `frame` still runs on top. A `null`
for a prop in `set_action_end`'s patch stops animating it.

**An animated number arrives with decimals**: 64 to 129 is 96.5 halfway, never rounded and never
snapped to `step`. A module that needs a whole number rounds it itself, or marks the prop
`animate: false` so no action ramps it. One that does neither —
`new Array(props.count)` is the usual case — throws on a fraction, so those frames draw the error
card, and an export stops there.

```js
export const meta = { name: "Bars", durationInFrames: 90 };
export const schema = {
  count: { type: "number", default: 5, min: 1, max: 20, step: 1 },
  accent: { type: "color", default: "#ff5a36" },
};

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const n = Math.round(props.count);
  const w = ctx.width / (2 * n);
  let bars = "";
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    bars += `<rect x="${(2 * i + 0.5) * w}" y="${ctx.height / 3}" width="${w}"
      height="${ctx.height / 3}" fill="${props.accent}"/>`;
  }
  return svg(ctx, bars);
}
```

A colour blends in OKLab with straight alpha, exactly as `interpolateColors` blends it: `#ff0000`
to `#0000ff` is `#8c53a2` halfway, not the muddy `#800080` of a channel-by-channel blend, and
`#ffffff` to `#00000000` is `#63636380`, grey and half transparent. While a prop
moves, every frame is drawn anew, so a graphic that had settled costs a full draw per frame for the
length of the action.

## Video inside a graphic: the matte

A graphic cannot read a video's pixels. To show video inside a shape the graphic draws, put the
graphic on the track directly above the video and switch that track to a **matte**: Track ▸ Matte
in the app, or `set_track {track, matte}` over MCP. A matte track's clips are never drawn. What
they show cuts the track directly behind: with `alpha`, the video shows where the graphic is
opaque; with `alpha_inverted`, where it is transparent; with `luma` and `luma_inverted`, by the
brightness of what it draws. `matte: "none"` turns it off. Where the matte track has no clip, the
video shows uncut. The module is written and called exactly as anywhere else. Fill the window in
white so it works in every mode, and animate it as usual: the cut follows each frame.

```js
export const meta = { name: "Window", durationInFrames: 90 };
export const schema = { radius: { type: "number", default: 24, min: 0, max: 200 } };

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const t = spring({ frame, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 18 });
  const w = ctx.width * 0.6 * t;
  const h = ctx.height * 0.6 * t;
  return svg(ctx, `<rect x="${(ctx.width - w) / 2}" y="${(ctx.height - h) / 2}"
    width="${w}" height="${h}" rx="${props.radius}" fill="#ffffff"/>`);
}
```

On a matte track a clip's position, scale, opacity, crop and actions still shape the window. Its
blend mode, drop shadow and reflection do nothing. The matted video's own drop shadow follows the
cut-out shape.

// app/Sources/GraphicTemplates.swift — the graphic modules the app bundles
// as templates (road map 10's G5b): `graphic/tests/graphics/*.js`, copied
// into `Contents/Resources/GraphicTemplates/` by project.yml's "Copy Graphic
// Templates" script. Insert ▸ Graphic… lists them by category
// (`GraphicCatalog.swift`, spec §11 G-45); inserting one writes it into the
// package's `graphics/` under a free name and places a clip drawn by it.
//
// **`list(in:)` compiles nothing**: it reads the folder, and a template's
// `title` here is its FILE STEM's. The browser's titles come from each
// template's `meta.name` (`GraphicTemplateLibrary` compiles them once, when
// the browser first opens); `title(for:)` is the fallback for a module with
// no `meta.name`. A missing folder lists nothing.

import Foundation

/// One bundled template: its module name (the file stem), its menu title
/// and where the file is.
struct GraphicTemplate: Equatable {
    let name: String
    let title: String
    let url: URL
}

enum GraphicTemplates {
    static let folderName = "GraphicTemplates"

    /// The folder beside `Fonts/` — `GraphicStore.manualDirectory`'s rule,
    /// so a probe that copies `Fonts/` next to itself can copy this too.
    static func directory(besideFonts fonts: URL) -> URL {
        GraphicStore.manualDirectory(besideFonts: fonts)
            .appendingPathComponent(folderName, isDirectory: true)
    }

    /// The app bundle's own.
    static var bundledDirectory: URL {
        directory(besideFonts: ProjectDocument.bundledFontsDirectory)
    }

    /// Every `*.js` in `directory` whose stem is a module name, sorted by
    /// name; `[]` when the folder is absent.
    static func list(in directory: URL) -> [GraphicTemplate] {
        let entries = (try? FileManager.default.contentsOfDirectory(
            at: directory, includingPropertiesForKeys: nil,
            options: [.skipsHiddenFiles])) ?? []
        return entries.compactMap { url -> GraphicTemplate? in
            guard url.pathExtension == "js" else { return nil }
            let name = url.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent
            guard GraphicStore.isModuleName(name) else { return nil }
            return GraphicTemplate(name: name, title: title(for: name), url: url)
        }.sorted { $0.name < $1.name }
    }

    /// "lower-third" → "Lower Third": split on "-", each part capitalised.
    static func title(for name: String) -> String {
        name.split(separator: "-").map { part in
            part.prefix(1).uppercased() + part.dropFirst()
        }.joined(separator: " ")
    }
